scenarios.given: Recording providers with distinct parent, configured/remote role, [subagents.models].general-purpose pin and agent-definition models; fresh goal attempts and isolated config for each routing case.
scenarios.when: Toggle current-model-only via env/config, change the parent model and trigger planner, strategist, skeptic and summary independently, including conflicting pins, valid explicit pairs and missing/invalid routes.
scenarios.then: The pinned-source planner fork uses the parent model with either switch state, ignoring configured planner pairs and general-purpose pins for verbatim history reuse. For non-fork strategist/skeptic requests, current-model-only removes explicit role overrides; the per-subagent pin then agent-definition model then parent determines the actual wire model. With the switch off, a valid configured role pair (or remote pair if absent) supplies an explicit override ahead of those pins. The summary has no per-role model key and uses the same general-purpose pin/definition/parent chain in either switch state. Assert each role separately against routingCases; InheritCurrent is not proof of unconditional parent routing.
scenarios.failure: Unavailable explicit pairs produce the source-described fail-open event and fall through to normal child selection; an invalid per-subagent pin warns before definition/parent fallback. A retryable explicit-pair spawn failure permits one retry without the role override, still subject to non-fork pin precedence; cancellation must not retry. Failed verification stays incomplete. These are pinned-source expectations only; frozen 1.0.34 routing remains unverified until measured, and any difference must be retained rather than hidden.

groups.rationale: Remote settings disk-cache disable is a real source-only config lifecycle control. Functional claim is cache IO/fetch behavior, not merely displaying false.

scenarios.given: An isolated remote-settings cache and recording config service.
scenarios.when: Start with cache enabled/disabled and stale/corrupt cache, then refresh and restart.
scenarios.then: Actual cache reads/writes and network refresh follow the control (false disables); effective provenance remains truthful and locked policy still wins.
scenarios.failure: Corrupt/unreadable cache and failed refresh cannot invent fresh settings or bypass policy.

groups.rationale: Literal lowercase container is a presence marker in the shared clipboard detector, suppressed by presence of DISPLAY/WAYLAND_DISPLAY. Pager caches this detector for OSC52 routing; native remains an attempted leg and Linux already emits OSC52 unless disabled. Source-only availability is not frozen runtime evidence.

scenarios.given: Fresh local/SSH/tmux terminal processes with controlled native and OSC52 clipboard helpers, no container sentinel files for env-isolation cases, and separate display markers.
scenarios.when: Vary lowercase container absent/empty/nonempty and uppercase CONTAINER independently, with DISPLAY/WAYLAND_DISPLAY absent or present (including empty); copy and inspect actual terminal bytes and clipboard delivery.
scenarios.then: Lowercase presence identifies a displayless container only when display markers and earlier sentinel conditions allow it; uppercase CONTAINER is distinct. Cached route enables OSC52 in the applicable non-Linux container case, while Linux already emits it; native remains attempted. The OSC52 disable override still wins over container/SSH/wrap routes.
scenarios.failure: Restart between cached-env variants; unavailable display/native clipboard, disabled OSC52 and failed delivery must not claim copy success. Frozen 1.0.34 behavior remains unverified until an isolated probe measures the route.

groups.rationale: Leading-underscore bwrap markers carry re-exec state and an encoded launch-time runtime-socket deny list between sandbox processes. They are not proven public frozen settings or a user-authorized bypass; trace marker validation and real confinement before any public parity claim. Existing sandbox effect contracts remain mandatory.

scenarios.given: Pinned sandbox re-exec and socket-deny consumers with isolated Linux filesystem/network canaries.
scenarios.when: Trace marker setting/consumption and encoded deny validation, then establish frozen availability before a controlled confinement probe.
scenarios.then: Record whether these are internal handoff only or an exposed frozen control; public behavior must get security-effect owners and real denial assertions rather than a config-display test.
scenarios.failure: Forged/malformed marker values cannot count as verified security or legitimate public config; unknown reachability stays discovery-only and existing sandbox requirements cannot be weakened.
